history.dynasty: Chera (tradition); Chola, Pandya, Vijayanagara, Madurai Nayak (renovations, traditional claims)
history.summary: Ancient Shiva-Amman temple in the heart of Dindigul city (Dindigul Bazaar). The moolavar is Padmagiriswarar (Shiva) with consort Abirami Amman, alongside a twin sanctum pair Kalahastheeswarar (Shiva) and Gnanambigai (Parvati). Legend: Mother Kali came to destroy the demon Analan; Shiva softened her fury and married her, and her beauty then earned her the name Abhirami ('the alluring one'); Brahma performed penance here and Shiva gave darshan from a lotus (Padma) tank, hence the name Padmagiriswarar. Tradition credits Chera kings with building the temple ~1000 years ago, with renovations by Cholas, Pandyas, Vijayanagara kings and Madurai Nayaks - all dynasty and period claims are tradition-based and unverified. A decorated 11-storey, 151-ft gopuram fronts the Dravidian-style complex; the temple was recently renovated. (flag) Coordinates are approximate: the geocoder repeatedly returns a differently-named shrine for the Dindigul Bazaar area; the temple is described as ~1 km from the Dindigul bus stand and in the city centre. name: Abirami Amman Temple
town_description: Dindigul is a city in central Tamil Nadu at the foot of its 900-ft rock fort, headquarters of the district. Its history centres on the fort, built in 1605 by the Madurai Nayaks after Chola, Pandya and Pallava phases; the Padmagiri hill gave the town its ancient names Padmagiri and Dindeeswaram.

travel.road: In Dindigul Bazaar in the city centre, off the Chennai-Theni highway (NH 44 corridor).
